label: rejected

evidence.V1: Lobed canopy on a trunk reads as a tree from front, three-quarter and silhouette; top view reads as a lumpy foliage blob - recognisable from all angles at 64 px.
evidence.V2: Only two big masses (canopy, trunk); branches are hidden or a tiny stub, no secondary canopy clumps, roots or bark detail - hierarchy is only partial.
evidence.V3: Generic lollipop proportion: straight uniform-width trunk with a boxy base, canopy is a single lobed blob; partly stylised but stiff.
evidence.V4: Canopy lobes are soft, but the trunk base is a hard stepped skirt with a sharp crease and dark band, and the branch stub at the fork is an abrupt dark notch - inconsistent.
evidence.V5: Canopy close-up shows a stair-stepped, notched vertex-colour boundary between the light crown and the darker lobes plus visible quad-grid faceting; trunk base has a hard crease and the fork shows a dark notch.
evidence.V6: Disciplined: foliage in two green values plus bark brown; autumn and blossom colourways keep the same structure.
evidence.V7: 1868 tris vs tree target 2000 (ceiling 5000) - under target.
evidence.V8: One white LF_VertexColor material and the hue rules match, but the jagged colour mask, grid faceting and boxy trunk flare miss the smooth fused-shell organic standard.
evidence.V9: Static scenery Studio line correct: Anchored, Hull (trunk-only part suggested for walk-through), CanTouch off, MeshPart white, SmoothPlastic, origin bottom-centre.

artifacts: Stair-stepped notched vertex-colour boundary on the canopy crown
Visible quad-grid faceting across canopy lobes
Hard stepped crease at trunk base flare
Dark notch where branch stub meets trunk under the canopy
top_fixes: Smooth the canopy colour transition (follow lobe contours or blend across more vertices) and add weighted normals / subdivision to remove grid faceting
Rebuild the trunk with a smooth root flare, taper and visible branch fork into the canopy
Break the canopy into 3-5 distinct clumps with a lighter top value so medium/small forms read
